classification.difficultyReason: Combine alternate angles on parallel lines with the triangle angle sum to justify a right angle.

content.prompt: Prove that $\triangle BEF$ is a right-angled triangle, giving full geometrical reasoning.

spec.description: Two parallel horizontal lines contain A–B–C and D–E–F–G. A transversal through E and B extends below E and above B to H; BF completes triangle BEF.
spec.mathematics: Matching parallel arrows; angle CBF is 35° and angle BEF is 55°. Coordinates derive these angles while preserving both transversal extensions.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible. The right angle at B and the angle at F are not supplied in the question diagram.

answer.short: $\angle BFE=35^{\circ}$ (alternate angles). Hence $\angle EBF=180^{\circ}-55^{\circ}-35^{\circ}=90^{\circ}$, so $\triangle BEF$ is right-angled at $B$.
answer.worked:
$\angle BFE=\angle CBF=35^{\circ}$ (alternate angles on parallel lines).

Using the angle sum of a triangle:
$$\begin{align*}
\angle EBF &= 180^{\circ}-55^{\circ}-35^{\circ}\\
\angle EBF &= 90^{\circ}.
\end{align*}$$
Therefore $\triangle BEF$ is right-angled at $B$.
